1
Introduction

Bakery commodities such as sponge cakes and fresh dairy cream pastries are perishable food matrices characterized by high water activity (aw ≥ 0.85), rich carbohydrates, and delicate butterfats. These biochemical conditions foster rapid bacterial proliferation, mold infestation, and volatile rancidity.

The Expiry Label Fallacy: Commercial bakeries rely on static printed "Best Before" dates. These labels assume uninterrupted refrigeration (4°C) and fail completely under retail ambient temperature abuse (25–35°C) or transport cold-chain breaks.

Conventional food testing relies on High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC), GC-MS, or microbial Petri culturing. While accurate, they require 24–48 hours of incubation, destructive sample grinding, and costly laboratory machinery (> $10,000).

NoseNet presents a non-invasive, autonomous IoT Electronic Nose. Utilizing an inverted top-mounted Bosch BME688 AI sensor operating at a 320°C MOX hotplate, NoseNet samples headspace Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) to deliver laboratory-grade freshness verdicts in under 60 seconds with zero food contact.

Figure 1: NoseNet Airtight Testing Chamber & Inverted Dome Sensor Assembly
2
Problem Statement

Modern bakeries, retailers, and food safety inspectors face three critical vulnerabilities in food quality assurance:

  • Invisibility of Early Microbial Spoilage: Bacterial acidification and fat souring emit volatile markers (ethanol, acetic acid, diacetyl) days before visual mold or discoloration appear.
  • Static Expiration Date Inadequacy: Pre-printed date codes cannot sense real-time microbial growth accelerated by ambient heat or humidity spikes.
  • Commercial Testing Inaccessibility: No affordable (< $35), portable, real-time volatile screening instrument exists for point-of-sale bakery quality enforcement.
Public Health Risk: Ingesting spoiled cream cakes containing Bacillus cereus or Staphylococcus aureus causes acute food-borne toxicosis.
3
Objectives & Technical Scope
  • Chamber Fabrication: Construct an airtight food-grade sampling chamber (120mm × 75mm) with an inverted dome mount for passive gaseous headspace equilibrium.
  • Dual-Mode Sensing: Interface ESP32-WROOM-32 with Bosch BME688 via I2C (0x76 @ 400 kHz) to record gas resistance (Rgas), temperature (T), humidity (RH), and pressure (P).
  • Thermal Stabilization: Implement a 5-second pulsed thermal pre-heat cycle (320°C) to clean sensor surfaces and calibrate clean baseline resistance (R0).
  • Deconvolution Algorithm: Develop relative resistance shift formulation (ΔR / R0) mapped to an empirical 4-tier freshness classification matrix.
  • Web BLE Dashboard: Build a progressive web dashboard streaming live telemetry over Web Bluetooth with SVG gas curves and audit exports.

System Architecture (Input • Processing • Output)

The system operates across three decoupled hardware and software layers:

1. INPUT LAYER
• Headspace Spoilage VOCs
• Ambient T (°C), RH (%), P (hPa)
• Raw Gas Resistance (Rgas)
2. PROCESSING
• ESP32 (240MHz, 520KB SRAM)
• 5-sec 320°C Hotplate Pulse
• Moving Avg & Baseline R0
• Shift: S = (ΔR/R0) × 100%
3. OUTPUT LAYER
• BLE GATT UART (Nordic NUS)
• Real-Time Next.js Web UI
• 4-Tier Freshness Status Card
• NDJSON & CSV Audit Logs

5
Algorithms & Techniques Used
A. MOX Chemisorption Sensing Physics:

At a hotplate temperature of 320°C, ambient atmospheric oxygen chemisorbs onto the metal-oxide surface by capturing electrons from the conduction band, creating a wide electron depletion barrier:

O2 (gas) + 2e− → 2O−(adsorbed)
• Result: Wide depletion layer; baseline gas resistance remains elevated (R0).

When microbial decomposition releases volatile reducing gases (ethanol, acetic acid, amines), these react with adsorbed oxygen, reinjecting trapped electrons into the conduction band:

VOC + O−(ads) → VOC-O + e−
• Result: Depletion barrier collapses; sensor resistance plunges drastically (Rgas ≪ R0).
B. Mathematical Shift Formulation:
S = [ (Rcomp − R0) / R0 ] × 100%
where Rcomp = baseline-compensated gas resistance, and R0 = specimen baseline resistance.
C. 4-Tier Freshness Classification Matrix:
Verdict Tier Shift Range (S) Score Biochemical Degradation State Retail Action
Fresh S ≥ −5.0% 90–100% Pristine crumb; baseline volatile equilibrium. Safe for sale
Fairly Fresh −15.0% ≤ S < −5.0% 70–89% Early moisture loss; minor volatile emergence. Prime consumption
Stale −35.0% ≤ S < −15.0% 40–69% Crumb retrogradation; noticeable lipid oxidation. Discount pricing
Spoiled S < −35.0% < 40% Severe bacterial souring; volatile ethanol/acids. Discard immediately
D. Specimen Baseline Registry (R0):
Normal Unfrozen: 36.80 kΩ
Normal Frozen: 46.80 kΩ
Pastry Unfrozen: 40.05 kΩ
Pastry Frozen: 40.62 kΩ

6
Conclusion & Longitudinal Results

A 7-day longitudinal study comprising 52 empirical records across 13 epochs (0h to 168h) was executed across Normal and Pastry cakes under Ambient (24–28°C) and Frozen (−18°C) environments:

Configuration 0h (Day 0) 72h (Day 3) 168h (Day 7) Final Shift Verdict
Pastry (Ambient) 40.05 kΩ 14.80 kΩ 7.90 kΩ −80.3% Spoiled
Pastry (Frozen) 40.62 kΩ 41.80 kΩ 41.60 kΩ +2.4% Fairly Fresh
Normal (Ambient) 36.80 kΩ 28.50 kΩ 23.90 kΩ −35.1% Stale
Normal (Frozen) 46.80 kΩ 46.90 kΩ 46.85 kΩ +0.1% Fresh
  • Critical Validation: Ambient Pastry Cake suffered an 80.3% resistance collapse due to rapid lactic/acetic acid souring in the dairy filling.
  • Cryogenic Stability: Sub-zero storage (−18°C) effectively arrested microbial metabolism, maintaining gas resistance stable (> 41.5 kΩ) over 168 hours.
  • Operational Metric: Achieved 100% classification fidelity across 52 trials with non-contact sampling in < 60s at ultra-low BOM cost (< $35).
Key Achievement: Confirms MOX gas resistance is an ultra-sensitive, non-destructive biochemical surrogate for food freshness and microbial degradation.
7
Future Enhancement
  • TinyML Edge AI: Deploy quantized 1D-CNN or Random Forest models on ESP32 via Edge Impulse / Bosch BSEC 2.0 for multi-analyte discrimination.
  • Heterogeneous Sensor Arrays: Integrate complementary MOS sensors (MQ-135, MQ-3, electrochemical cells) to broaden classification to meat, poultry, and seafood.
  • Blockchain Cold-Chain: Automate MQTT telemetry uploads with decentralized QR-code cold-chain passports for tamper-proof retail distribution tracking.
  • Handheld Wand Form-Factor: Miniaturize the enclosure into a pen-type battery-operated inspection wand with an OLED screen for field safety inspectors.
